name: Solo Whist
description: Solo Whist (or simply 'Solo') is a British trick-taking card game derived from Whist but incorporating bidding elements from Boston and Quadrille. Unlike Partnership Whist, players bid individually to achieve specific goals, such as making 5, 9, or 13 tricks alone ('Solo', 'Abundance', 'Abundance Declared') or losing every trick ('Misere'). It is a game of high skill and nerve.

overview.description: Solo Whist (or simply 'Solo') is a British trick-taking card game derived from Whist but incorporating bidding elements from Boston and Quadrille. history.origins: Developed in the mid-19th century from Ghent Whist (Belgium). Became wildly popular in British social clubs.
timeline: Present: Still played in UK leagues, though less than Bridge.
history.cultural: Often played for small stakes. 'Going a bundle' means bidding 13 tricks.
history.evolution: The 'Prop and Cop' partnership bid (Proposal and Acceptance) is unique to Solo Whist, allowing temporary alliances.

setup.players: Four players, each ultimately playing for themselves, though they form temporary alliances (one against three or two against two) for each hand.
setup.deck: A standard 52-card pack is used; cards in each suit rank from high to low: A K Q J 10 9 8 7 6 5 4 3 2.
setup.dealing: Deal 13 cards each in packets of three until four cards remain, then deal the last four singly; the last card (to the dealer) is turned face up to indicate prospective trump. Dealer may pick it up after the first trick if not played.

rules.objective: Win your bid: in Prop and Cop make 8 tricks with your partner (turned suit as trump); in Solo make 5 tricks alone in the turned suit; in Misère lose every trick (no trumps); in Abundance make 9 tricks alone (you choose trump); in Abundance Declared make all 13 tricks (no trumps, you lead). Settle in units after each deal.
rules.gameplay: Deal 13 cards each; last card to dealer is turned for prospective trump. Bid in order from dealer's left: Prop, Cop, Solo, Misère, Abundance, Abundance in Trumps, Misère Ouverte, Abundance Declared. Higher bid wins; bidding continues until three players pass. If all pass or Prop finds no Cop, redeal. Play: player to dealer's left leads (except Abundance Declared when bidder leads). Follow suit if possible; highest trump wins the trick, else highest card of the led suit. Winner of each trick leads to the next.
keyRules: Follow suit if you can; otherwise play any card.
Highest trump in the trick wins; if no trump, highest card of the led suit wins.
Prop and Cop: two players try to make 8 tricks with turned suit as trump.
Solo: one player tries to make 5 tricks alone. Misère: one player tries to lose every trick.

strategy.basic: In a Solo bid (5 tricks), you need 3-4 trumps and a couple of side Aces. Don't bid Misere unless you have 2s, 3s, and voids in dangerous suits. In Prop/Cop, communicate with your partner via discards.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Misere' Defense: Defenders must lead a suit the Misere player is void in (if known) or force them to play high. If the Misere player plays a King, you must play under it to let them win.
strategy.advanced: Leading trumps against a Solo: Usually bad unless you have many. Better to force the Soloist to ruff (trump) your winning Aces in side suits to reduce their trump length.
tips: Prop and Cop is the only partnership bid.
Misere is the most tense bid.

variations.name: Straight Solo
variations.description: Prop and Cop eliminated; only individual bids (Solo and above) are allowed.

variations.name: Single round of bidding
variations.description: Each player has only one opportunity to bid except: dealer's left may Cop after passing if only bid was Prop; a player whose Prop was not accepted may raise to Solo.

scoring.description: Fixed payments for each bid (e.g., Solo pays 2 chips, Abundance pays 4).
